name: Emirates Investment Bank
founded: 1976 (incorporated 17 Feb 1976 in Dubai by decree of the Ruler of Dubai; founded by three UAE business families; private banking strategy since 2008)
ownership_summary: Subsidiary of Al Futtaim Private Company LLC, which holds 92.39% (30 Jun 2026 and 31 Dec 2025). The 7.61% free float is held by individuals, and the shares have been listed on DFM since 2005 with very limited trading in 2025. One director holds an indirect 15% interest through Al Futtaim Private Co. LLC (governance report 2025).
government_link: No. Privately controlled by the Al Futtaim family group (Al Futtaim Private Company LLC, 92.39%) (S1, S3).
group_structure: Standalone bank with a CBUAE restricted banking licence (since 2023) and SCA licences for promotion, financial consultation and financial analysis, and investment and portfolio management (S3). Its small associate stake (AED 72 thousand) was sold to a related party in H1 2026 (S1). Part of the Al Futtaim group, which supplies some services (IT data centre lease and outsourcing, office lease) (S3).
footprint: UAE only: head office in Festival Tower, Dubai Festival City (S14). Clients include HNW individuals from the region and abroad. The 2026 plan includes 'exploration of a flagship presence in the UAE' (S2).
customer_segments: High-net-worth and internationally mobile individuals and families (private banking); Independent Asset Managers (IAMs) through a dedicated team (S6, S9).
business_lines: Private banking and wealth management: active advisory and discretionary portfolio management (global multi-asset), open-architecture mutual funds platform, global trading and execution, custody, Lombard and real-estate-secured lending, wealth and estate planning (trusts and foundations via external experts), daily banking and deposits, IAM services. Treasury runs a mainly investment-grade bond portfolio (S2, S6, S7, S8, S9).

capabilities.wealth_summary: EIBank is a small, Al Futtaim-controlled, DFM-listed private bank in Dubai (AED 4.55bn balance sheet at 30 Jun 2026) serving HNW clients and Independent Asset Managers. Total client assets were AED 10.99bn at end 2025 (deposits AED 3.31bn plus custody/fiduciary assets AED 7.68bn). It offers active advisory and discretionary multi-asset portfolios managed in-house, an open-architecture mutual funds platform, global trading and execution, custody, Lombard lending and wealth/estate planning. In 2025 it began a multi-year transformation to become a 'digital private banking institution'. In Oct 2025 it chose Avaloq's platform (core wealth platform, RM Workplace, web and mobile banking, Community APIs). New leadership with private-banking backgrounds arrived (CEO Michel Longhini, ex-FAB Group Head of Private Banking; director Christophe de Backer, ex-Edmond de Rothschild). A refreshed brand and renewed private banking proposition are planned for 2026.

segments.name: Independent Asset Managers (IAM)
segments.eligibility: Not published; dedicated multi-lingual RM team

private_banking.detail: Core business: relationship-led private banking for HNW clients. Strategy (2025-26) is a 'digital-first, customer-centric private banking experience', with a renewed proposition and brand in 2026.

asset_management.detail: In-house Asset Management team (Head: Asad Khan) runs active advisory and discretionary global multi-asset strategies and model portfolios; an Investment Committee sets the house view. SCA licence for investment and portfolio management. AUM not disclosed.

brokerage.detail: Trading and execution platform with global market access; also offered to IAMs. Custody of client assets (AED 7.28bn fiduciary assets at 30 Jun 2026).

digital_investing.detail: Online banking portal exists (online.eibank.com); a new web and mobile banking solution is being implemented on Avaloq (announced Oct 2025). No in-app investing features documented yet.

advisory.detail: Active Advisory service with tailored proposals and periodic rebalancing ideas; SCA licence for financial consultation and analysis.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management under agreed mandates or specified model portfolios across fixed income, equities, real estate, commodities, alternatives and cash.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Model portfolios managed by the Asset Management team and overseen by the Investment Committee; no robo-advice.

funds_platform.detail: Open-architecture mutual funds platform (conventional and alternative strategies) from curated global managers; platform provider not named. Also available to IAMs.

structured_products.detail: Not mentioned on the solutions or asset management pages.

private_markets.detail: Discretionary strategies include 'alternatives' and the funds platform covers 'alternative strategies'; the bank holds managed funds and private equities on its own book. No named private-markets client product.

partners.what: Avaloq core wealth platform, RM Workplace, Web and Mobile Banking and Community APIs to consolidate front, middle and back office; implementation under way (system under development capitalised in the accounts)
Data centre lease and IT outsourcing (related-party transactions)

initiatives.what: CFO Kishore Venkat appointed interim CEO (CBUAE-confirmed) while a permanent CEO was recruited
Christophe de Backer (ex-Group CEO Edmond de Rothschild) elected independent director
Avaloq selected for core wealth platform, RM Workplace, web/mobile banking and APIs

Multi-year transformation launched to reposition as a digital private bank: new technology architecture, AI-enabled RM tools, expanded product platform; 2026 plans for a refreshed brand, renewed private banking proposition and a possible UAE flagship
Transformation ongoing: AED 42.7m of intangible assets purchased in H1 2026, outstanding system-transformation commitments of AED 45.0m, G&A up 99% year on year

opportunities: Explicit strategy to become a digital-first private bank, with an expanded product platform 'to provide access to best-in-class global solutions' and AI-enabled RM tools (directors' report FY2025, S2).
Avaloq deployment includes Community APIs for connecting third-party services, a natural integration route for an external product shelf (S12).
New CEO and board members with international private-banking backgrounds; 2026 relaunch of brand and proposition (S2, S4, S3).
Serves Independent Asset Managers with platform access, an additional distribution channel (S9).
barriers: Core and digital stack recently committed to Avaloq (front, middle, back office and web/mobile), so a white-label platform overlap is unlikely; fit is more likely as products or AI agents via APIs (S12, S1).
Small balance sheet with sharply lower profit during the transformation (H1 2026 net profit AED 11.1m vs 49.3m) may limit new spend (S1).
Asset management, model portfolios and an open-architecture funds platform are already in-house (S7).
incumbent_vendors: Avaloq: core wealth platform, RM Workplace, web/mobile banking, Community APIs (announced 23 Oct 2025, S12)
